title: Video shows baseball players and fans evacuating field as 7.2 earthquake hits Venezuela
content:
In a scene reminiscent of what became known as the “Earthquake Series” in 1989, video captured on Wednesday showed players, coaches and fans scrambling to safety during a professional baseball game in Venezuela, which was rocked by two powerful temblors that struck in rapid succession.

The first of the two quakes — which was epicentered 100 miles west of the capital city of Caracas, where the baseball game was being played — registered 7.2 on the Richter scale. It struck in the middle of an at-bat. Following a 1-2 pitch in the top of the first inning, a batter signals a timeout to the home plate umpire, and the official and the catcher quickly remove their masks.  After a moment of confusion, the game came to a halt and the video shows fans and players spilling onto the field.

The camera capturing the images also relayed the shaking. At the same time, light poles surrounding the ballpark could be seen swaying, and the stadium’s public address system appeared to tremble as the camera cut to footage of two helmets. Another quake struck 39 seconds later, registering at a magnitude of 7.5.

As of mid-Thursday, at least 164 people have been killed and nearly 1,000 injured in what is being described as the country’s most powerful earthquake in more than a century, according to Venezuela’s acting President, Delcy Rodriguez. Videos posted on social media also show collapsed residential towers in Caracas and in the nearby port city of La Guaira, where more than 100 buildings were destroyed, according to the United Nations’ main humanitarian agency.

The scene on the field recalled images of the 1989 World Series between the Oakland Athletics and the host San Francisco Giants. As the teams prepared for Game 3 of that series, the 6.9-magnitude Loma Prieta Earthquake shook the Bay Area. Players from both teams rushed to the stands in their uniforms to escort family and friends to the playing field, all while fans at a packed Candlestick Park looked on.
